replies.author: Hulk
replies.text:
ieVai2 NetGuard is fully compatible with GrapheneOS.

The way Data Saver mode works makes sense. If you don't want to use Mobile Data at all, then turn off Mobile Data.

replies.author: Hulk
replies.text: Also, some apps have their own internal options to further restrict/minimize mobile data usage.

replies.author: Uphill1945
replies.text: Is there another solution that doesn't require a VPN or Proxy?

replies.author: other8026
replies.text:
Uphill1945

I'm assuming you're asking if it's possible to restrict network access to apps based on the kind of network you're connected to? If so, then no, there is no way to do that in GrapheneOS.

For many who want to preserve their privacy, using a VPN all the time should be sufficient, even if connectivity stays the same across different networks. Or, as Hulk suggested, just turn off mobile data in the network settings.

replies.author: Uphill1945
replies.text: other8026 it's more like I don't want system updater eating up all my data when I'm going places. That kinda stuff

replies.author: DeletedUser29
replies.text:
Uphill1945 You can limit system updates to only use wifi.

Settings > System > System update > Permitted network > set to Unmetered

replies.author: DeletedUser29
replies.text:
Uphill1945 To clarify what the Permitted network options do, here's the official usage guide explanation:

The "Permitted networks" setting controls which networks will be used to perform updates. It defaults to using any network connection. It can be set to "Non-roaming" to disable it when the cellular service is marked as roaming or "Unmetered" to disable it on cellular networks and also Wi-Fi networks marked as metered.

https://grapheneos.org/usage#updates-settings

replies.author: IAMHereNow288
replies.text:
I have seen Android builds that do this, allowing for mobile data access / WiFi access to be allowed/disallowed via their respective toggles within an app's network permissions.

This is a feature that I would value having on GrapheneOS. I too use the data saver, but I'd like greater ability to restrict mobile data access for certain apps by turning it off for them altogether, while keeping it on for others. Useful in situations where there is low-data available, such as when roaming with certain carriers.

replies.author: tilion_silverbow
replies.text:
Resurrecting this thread. I know it isn't currently possible to do this, but could it ever be? Is it a difficult problem to solve?

There might be use-cases for the privacy and/or security of restricting an app's access to mobile data. However, I'm coming at this from the angle of not having unlimited data -- I use Netguard to allow only my most necessary apps to access mobile data so that I don't burn through my low monthly limits.

It would be great if there was an option to do this directly in an app's settings rather than via Netguard, i.e. just split the "Networks" permission into "WiFi" and "Mobile Data," or something like that. For one, it'd allow me to use a VPN when on mobile data, since currently Netguard takes up the VPN spot when active. Not thinking about needing to start up Netguard every time I leave WiFi would be a plus, too. (It's just a couple clicks, I guess, but no clicks are better than a couple)

replies.author: tilion_silverbow
replies.text:
I take back my above post, because I wasn't really familiar enough with Data Saver. It appears that while Data Saver is turned on, then any app that is 1) not open and 2) has not been whitelisted manually will have no access to mobile data. As long as you don't open a blacklisted app while on mobile data, this doesn't appear functionally different to Netguard.

Open to being corrected if I've misunderstood something.
